findings: AO-MA-10j wires high-risk supersession evidence into the ao-release-gate required-check path without making AI output release authority.
The self-reference problem is avoided by committing only raw head_sha-free reviewer evidence and generating the head-bound supersession artifact at CI runtime from trusted base code.

Fail-closed behavior is preserved: partial raw reviewer pairs, provider mismatch, scope mismatch, malformed evidence, stale or unavailable git context, and authority boundary flips all deny rather than pass.

Workflow changes are additive and do not mutate CODEOWNERS, branch protection, rulesets, testai/smee/webhooks, Vault, GitHub App credentials, support scope, production claim, or live adapter execution.
Claude independent review returned AGREE and noted only non-blocking concerns; the root review dependency and fetch fail-closed behavior were documented in the workflow after review.
CI follow-up scopes the older AO-MA-10h no-workflow-mutation introducer invariant to its original contract-only slice, while AO-MA-10j explicitly owns required-check workflow wiring.
